subject: Post-demo: NovaHealth deployment options + indicative pricing
content:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Graves <eliot@novahealth.io>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novahealth.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: NovaHealth deployment options + indicative pricing

Hi Eliot / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a few next steps so we can get you a scoped quote that matches your constraints. I captured the high-level notes below; please flag anything I missed.

Summary of your requirements (from call)
- Primary use case: real-time clinician-assist prompts (avg request size ~200 tokens, peak concurrency ~150 RTP requests/sec).
- Data sensitivity: PHI present in prompts and responses for a subset of flows — need SOC 2 + option for VPC/bring-your-own-key.
- Latency SLO: 250ms p95 for short completions (≤128 tokens).
- Cost sensitivity: want to understand per-month committed cost vs pay-as-you-go tradeoffs for 100k–1M monthly completions.

Deployment pathways we discussed
1) Hosted API (fastest, no infra ops)
   - Best for quick POC and lower ops burden.
   - Pricing: per-token usage (we provided examples during demo). For your workload, ballpark run-rate estimate: $8k–$22k/month depending on QPS distribution and caching.
   - Pros: immediate start, managed security baseline.
   - Cons: you'd need to confirm encryption/KMS restrictions for PHI.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools)
   - Predictable throughput via reserved units; supports private model pinning and stronger isolation.
   - Pricing: monthly reserved commit + metered overage. Example: 2x reserved A100-equivalent pools to hit your 150 req/sec target with caching = ~$55k/month committed (with 12-month discount options). Effective per-completion unit cost can be lower than Hosted at volume.
   - Pros: cost predictability, SLA, peak performance, and easier compliance attachments for enterprise procurement.
   - Cons: commit required; lead time for capacity provisioning.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem integration)
   - For full control, BYO keys, and air-gapped requirements. We can ship a private control plane and agent deployment for on-prem inference.
   - Pricing: platform license + infra ownership. Early estimate: platform fee ~$20k/mo + infra amortized (depends on your hardware choices).
   - Pros: maximum data control and compliance fit.
   - Cons: longer onboarding, ops handoff.

Requested next items from us
- A short spreadsheet with 3 modeled scenarios: POC (hosted, low volume), Production reserved (2x dedicated pools, 12-mo commit), Private VPC (platform + infra sizing).
- Draft quote showing banded committed pricing and per-token equivalents to compare apples-to-apples.
- Compliance note about PHI handling options and KMS integrations.

I've attached a lightweight draft that combines a sizing worksheet + a first-pass quote (NovaHealth-RI-draft-quote-0326.pdf). That file contains the assumptions we used for the numbers below.

Proposed next steps
- I'll loop Vivek (our infra lead) on the sizing/detail work and ask him to surface any gating items for dedicated/private.
- Can we tentatively schedule a 30-min follow-up on Tue 3/30 to walk the numbers with your ops + procurement?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

-----

On Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700, Eliot Graves <eliot@novahealth.io> wrote:

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the recap. Couple clarifying notes from our side:
- PHI scope: about ~20% of traffic includes PHI. For POC we can sanitize, but production will need KMS + shared responsibility controls.
- On throughput: 150 RPS is the peak for one region; we may route read-only flows to another region later.
- Procurement asks: can you provide a 12-month committed price and a 36-month amortized private option (we need the numbers for our finance team).

Please include a short line item for a trial period (we'd like a 30-day evaluation with a low-cost reserved window to validate latency).

—Eliot

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eliot Graves <eliot@novahealth.io>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@novahealth.io>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: NovaHealth deployment options + indicative pricing

Vivek —

Looping you in to help size dedicated pools and confirm the feasibility of a 30-day reserved trial. Key ask from NovaHealth:
- Achieve p95 ≤250ms for ≤128-token completions at peak 150 RPS in one region.
- 20% PHI in traffic; customer requires KMS + SOC2 evidence (we have SOC2, but need to surface docs).
- Wants 12-month committed pricing + 36-month amortized private option.

Attachments: novahealth-resource-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (short worksheet with their provided QPS and token distribution).

Can you:
1) Put together two committed sizing/pricing buckets (conservative and aggressive) and a recommended config for a 30-day reserved trial (what capacity we need to reserve for the trial).
2) Call out any compliance gating (e.g., KMS key trust boundaries, required contracts).
3) Quick note if a VPC/private pilot could be staged in 8–12 weeks and rough platform fee/infra assumptions for 36-month amortization.

Happy to sync if you want to walk through the worksheet.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Eliot Graves <eliot@novahealth.io>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@novahealth.io>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: NovaHealth deployment options + indicative pricing

Camila / Eliot / Maya —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the worksheet and put together a concise cost model (attached in the draft quote PDF). High-level takeaways below.

30-day reserved trial feasibility
- Trial config to meet p95 ≤250ms at 150 RPS: 2x dedicated inference pools (A100-equivalent), with autoscale headroom disabled for the trial window to keep costs bounded. Estimated trial commit = ~$6,500 for 30 days (covers reserved pool time + basic monitoring).

12-month committed options (two buckets)
- Conservative (baseline): 2x pools sustained with small burst capacity — commit ~$55k/month (12-mo).
- Aggressive (headroom): 3x pools to cover growth and regional failover — commit ~$80k/month (12-mo).
- Effective per-completion cost: depends on utilization; at ~70% sustained utilization conservative option ~ $0.005/token-equivalent for a 128-token average completion. Hosted per-token examples from demo were ~ $0.008–$0.015/token for similar output complexity.

Private VPC / on-prem (36-mo amortization)
- Platform license: ~$18k/month (platform + support).
- Infra: assuming 2x A100-class nodes fully dedicated — CAPEX amortized over 36 months + networking = approx $28k–$42k/month depending on vendor/hardware choices.
- Total approx: $46k–$60k/month (platform + infra amortized) — note: this excludes facilities/Ops headcount.

Compliance and gating items
- SOC2: we can provide SOC2 report and a redacted evidence package for procurement.
- KMS: supported. For VPC/on-prem we recommend customer-managed KMS (HSM) — requires key-exchange agreement and minimal integration work (1–2 weeks).
- Data residency: can run regional dedicated pools in your requested region; cross-region failover adds cost.

Next suggested steps
1) Camila: send an updated draft quote with three banded options (POC trial / 12-mo conservative / 12-mo aggressive) and a parallel 36-mo private amortized line.
2) Eliot: confirm if procurement wants a formal SOC2 package + an NDA for KMS exchange.
3) Tentative follow-up: Tue 30 Mar, 30-min to review quote and trial schedule. I can join to walk throughput tradeoffs.

If you want, I can also produce a short table translating committed monthly costs into a per-completion "apples-to-apples" metric to make finance comparisons easier.

-Vivek

Redwood Inference — Infrastructure & Performance
vivek@redwood.ai
